title: review: P2b fix round 1 applied on task/T-0466 at c6c17c1 (reply worker handles held, refused and incompatible outcomes; resume_plan single source; compat change falls back to fresh on the fix task) — re-review of T-0466 after T-0478 request_changes, security checklist on (daemon.py, executor.py)
spec: Review the diff of task/T-0466 (head c6c17c1, two commits over goal/T-0445 at 29606ef: 21c34a7 P2b and c6c17c1 the fix round) against the T-0466 acceptance criteria and the T-0478 findings: (1) _dispatch_reply_worker handles every executor.reply status (done, failed, held with requeue by clearing dispatched_at and its _done marker, refused as parent_merged, incompatible falling back to a fresh dispatch on the fix task, exceptions) and always posts a result on the fix task; (2) executor.resume_plan is the single compatibility source used by dispatch and reply; (3) parent thread bookkeeping (codex_thread, codex_thread_head, rounds) changes only on an actual resume; (4) the five T-0479 tests and five T-0466 tests exist and pass; (5) security checklist for daemon.py and executor.py (no argv injection from failure text, no unbounded reads, locks preserved). Verdict approve or request_changes with path:line comments.
acceptance: verdict approve or request_changes with path:line comments on every T-0478 finding and the security checklist

comments.issue: In `_run`, `log_task = task.get("_run_task_id", task["id"])` was introduced so `bus.log_run` attributes fix-round runs to the fix task (line 122, 142, 146 all use `log_task`), but the sibling `bus.update(task["id"], status="held", hold_reason=f"codex usage limit; resets in {secs // 60} min", ...)` on this line still uses `task["id"]`, which for a fix-round reply is the PARENT's id (since `reply()` sets `t = {**t, "_run_task_id": fix_round_task_id, ...}` but `t["id"]` stays the parent's real id from `bus.get(task_id)`). Hitting a codex usage limit mid fix-round resume therefore overwrites the parent task's `status`/`hold_reason` (e.g. clobbering "gate_red" with "codex usage limit..."), even though the fix task's own held/budget state is separately and correctly recorded by `_dispatch_reply_worker`'s `elif r["status"] == "held":` branch via `bus.post_result`/`clear_stage`. Same pattern at line 124 (`bus.update(task["id"], resume_hint=...)` on argv error) and at reply()'s own early returns (executor.py:352-355 rounds-exhausted sets `status="failed"` on the parent id, and 358-360 sets `status="held", hold_reason="executor ... unavailable"` on the parent id).

`bus.update(task_id, status="failed", reason=f"fix loop exceeded {MAX_ROUNDS} rounds; escalate or re-spec")` runs with `task_id` bound to the parent's id when called via the new `fix_round_task_id=`/`plan=` path (daemon.py `_dispatch_reply_worker` calls `executor.reply(parent_id, delta, fix_round_task_id=task_id, plan=plan)`). If this branch is ever reached for a fix round (e.g. rounds incremented by a concurrent caller between `resume_plan`'s check and this increment), it force-fails the PARENT task directly instead of the fix task, bypassing the fix task's own `bus.post_result` bookkeeping that the rest of this feature relies on.

`test_reply_worker_handles_held_requeues_fix_task_for_retry` stubs out `executor.reply` entirely (`self.swap(executor, "reply", reply)`), so it never exercises the real `reply()`/`_run()` internals where the parent-id status clobbering described above actually lives; the test's `assertIsNone(bus.get(parent).get("result"))` doesn't check `status`/`hold_reason`, so it would pass even with the bug present. None of the added tests call the real `reply()` through a simulated codex usage-limit or rounds-exhausted event with `fix_round_task_id` set, so this regression has no coverage.
